1.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh tells Ezekiel to speak a prophecy. Ezekiel is to speak to Mount Seir, but the message is for all of the people of Edom.

This is an idiom that is used to introduce something that God told his prophets or his people. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 3:16. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke this message] or [Yahweh spoke these words]

2.note: God calls Ezekiel this to emphasize that Ezekiel is only a human being. God is eternal and powerful, but humans are not. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [Mortal person] or [Human]

2.q: set your face against Mount Seir
2.note: Mount Seir was far away, so Ezekiel could not see it, but Yahweh commands him to stare in that direction as a symbol of harming the people there. See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 6:2. Alternate translation: [turn toward Mount Seir and stare] or [stare toward Mount Seir so that the people there will be harmed]

2.q: Mount Seir and prophesy against it
2.note: “the mountain of Seir.” Yahweh tells Ezekiel to speak to Mount Seir as if it could hear him. The message is for all of the people of Edom. Alternate translation: [Mount Seir and prophesy against it because of what the people of Edom have done]

3.note: Alternate translation: [to the mountain] or [to the people of Edom]

3.q: Behold! I am against you, Mount Seir, and I will strike you with my hand and make you a desolation and a waste
3.note: Yahweh tells Ezekiel to speak to Mount Seir as if it could hear him. The message is for all of the people of Edom. Alternate translation: [Listen, Mount Seir, I will strike you with my hand and make you a desolation and a waste because of what your people did]
The word “Behold” here adds emphasis to what follows. Alternate translation: [Listen!] or [Indeed!]
Alternate translation: [I am your enemy] or [I oppose you]

3.q: I will strike you with my hand
3.note: Here “hand” represents power. Alternate translation: [I will use my power to strike you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **desolation**, you can express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: [make you desolate]

4.note: When Yahweh says that people will know that he is Yahweh, he is implying that they will know that he is the one true God who has supreme authority and power. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 6:7. Alternate translation: [understand that I am Yahweh, the one true God] or [realize that I, Yahweh, have supreme power and authority]

5.q: you poured them out into the hands of the sword
5.note: This metaphor could mean: (1) “you gave them over to their enemies who killed them with swords” or (2) “you killed them with swords.”

5.q: at the time of their distress
5.note: Alternate translation: [at a time of disaster]

6.q: I will prepare you for bloodshed
6.note: Here “bloodshed” is a metonym for killing. Alternate translation: [I will make it easy for your enemies to kill many of you]
Here “bloodshed” is a metonym for killing. Yahweh speaks of bloodshed as if it were a person who could chase them. Alternate translation: [your enemies will chase you down and kill you]

6.q: Since you did not hate bloodshed
6.note: Here “bloodshed” is a metonym for killing. Alternate translation: [Since you did not hate it when enemies brutally killed the people of Israel]

Yahweh is following the custom of the culture by swearing an oath to indicate the seriousness of what he is saying. According to the custom, people would guarantee the oath by something that they hold sacred, and the most sacred thing would be the life of Yahweh. To do the same, Yahweh is swearing by his own life in the first part of this verse. After stating what he will do, He then follows the custom to state the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”), which would be the penalty for not telling the truth. Normally the penalty would be understood to be something general such as “may Yahweh punish me severely,” yielding something like, “If you did not hate blood, may Yahweh punish me severely…” But since Yahweh is speaking, stating this would not make sense. It may be clearest to translate the oath as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [I swear that it is because you hated blood]

Here, **blood** stands for the life of the people that the Edomites killed. It may also refer to the fact that the Israelites and the Edomites were related, tracing their ancestry to the brothers Jacob and Esau, respectively. Alternate translation: [If you did not hate the life of others] or [If you did not hate killing your kinsmen]

7.q: when I cut off from it anyone who passes through and returns again
7.note: This could mean: (1) “cut off” is a metaphor that means to destroy. Alternate translation: [I will destroy anyone who enters it or leaves it] or (2) [cut off] is a metaphor that means to stop someone from doing something. Alternate translation: [I will make it so that people do not travel back and forth through it]

8.q: those who were killed by the sword
8.note: Here “sword” represents enemies who fought them in battle. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 31:17. Alternate translation: [those whom enemies have killed with swords] or [those who have died in battle] (See also: [Metonymy](ta:figs-metonymy))

9.note: “desolate forever.” This may be an exaggeration to emphasize the destruction.

9.q: Your cities will not be inhabited
9.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. This may be an exaggeration for emphasis. Alternate translation: [People will not live in your cities] (See also: [Hyperbole](ta:figs-hyperbole))
Here “you” is plural. God is speaking to the people of Mount Seir, rather than to a single mountain.

10.note: The word “You” refers to the mountain of Seir. Ezekiel is to speak to the mountain as if it can hear him. The message is for the people of Edom. Alternate translation: [Your people said]
Alternate translation: [the lands of Israel and Judah]
The word “mine” can be stated in plural form. Alternate translation: [will become ours]
The word “we” refers to the people of Edom.

10.q: even when Yahweh was present with them
10.note: It is implied that Yahweh was protecting Israel and Judah. Alternate translation: [but Yahweh was there protecting Israel and Judah]

11.q: I will do according to your anger and according to your jealousy
11.note: This could mean: (1) “I will punish you because of your anger and jealousy” or (2) “just as you acted against the people of Israel with anger and jealousy, I will act against you with anger and jealousy.”

12.note: Here “mountains” represents the whole land of Israel.
This phrase can be stated in active form. Alternate translation: [They are in ruins]

12.q: they have been given over to us to devour
12.note: The people of Mount Seir taking the land of Israel and using it for themselves is spoken of as if they were wild animals that would devour the mountains of Israel. Alternate translation: [they are here for us to devour] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

14.note: This can be stated in first person. Alternate translation: [This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say]

14.q: I will make you a desolation
14.note: Here “you” refers to Mount Seir, but the message is for the people of Edom. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **desolation**, you can express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: [Because of what your people did I will make you desolate] (See also: [Abstract Nouns](ta:figs-abstractnouns))

Here “earth” represents the people of the earth. The word “entire” is a generalization that refers only to people near Mount Seir. Alternate translation: [people who know that I have destroyed you rejoice]

15.q: As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the people of Israel because of its desolation
15.note: This speaks of the land that Yahweh gave to the Israelites as their inheritance. Alternate translation: [As you rejoiced when I made the land of the Israelites desolate]

15.q: I will do the same to you
15.note: This could mean: (1) “I will make your land desolate” or (2) “I will rejoice when your land is desolate” or (3) “I will make other people rejoice because of your desolation.”
The word **they** possibly refers to (1) “the people of the earth” or (2) “the people of Israel and Judah.”
